Dropping connection." and the subscriber code; answerer mgruhler explains the version cause and the reporter posts the change that resolved it.

E2.evidence: The publisher (franka_state_controller from franka_ros, run in franka_control) and the reporter's own subscriber node /MoveRobot ("No this Node is my own, because i need some data from the robot for my application.") are separate units interacting through the topic /franka_state_controller/franka_states of type franka_msgs/FrankaState. The two sides carry different franka_msgs/FrankaState definitions (md5 ed28b9cb... vs 7782ef1d...). The resolving change is a CMakeLists.txt find_package edit, but its effect is to rebuild the consumer against the provider's changed definition, which the tree counts as an interface change, not build-only.

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: the running publisher comes from the reporter's source build of current franka_ros ("i rebuild the full current franka_ros package yesterday"), whose FrankaState gained robot_mode after release 0.6.0 (commit 3991f55, 2018-08-24, unreleased until 0.7.0 in 2020); the subscriber was compiled against a FrankaState whose md5 equals the 0.6.0 definition. Answerer: "This is usually the case when messages change between versions. FrankaState actually changed a while back and this change hasn't been released yet."

resolution.summary: Rebuild the subscriber against the franka_msgs that the running franka_ros build uses, by adding franka_msgs to find_package(catkin REQUIRED COMPONENTS ...) in the subscriber's CMakeLists.txt. The answerer's general recommendation: "You should clone and compile the full franka_ros package or use it entirely from debians, whatever makes more sense for you."
resolution.evidence: Reporter: "I find the solution: I forget to rework the CMakeList.txt to add the line franka_msgs in the find_package part" followed by the find_package block and "Thank you for all your help." (https://answers.ros.org/question/318190/). The provider revision in the resolved composition is the same source build (date-derived, see revision_basis). The answerer doubted the mechanism: "even though this is required for the code to compile, this should not lead to the problem of shown above... franka_msgs was obviously found, otherwise it could not have been included in your code. How remains a mystery to me, however :-)"

notes: Direction: the error is printed by the publisher ("our version has" 7782ef1d...), and the client /MoveRobot requests ed28b9cb.... Computing the genmsg md5 of franka_msgs/FrankaState at repository revisions gives ed28b9cbecdc83fa7d31efb59f1ce010 at 0.5.0 and 0.6.0 (the definition is unchanged from 29ed2e3/9b3e4c8, 2018-01-29, until 3991f55), and 7782ef1d208d3efc42f6a4cc3c41c065 from 3991f55 (2018-08-24, which added the ROBOT_MODE_* constants and 'uint8 robot_mode') until fb431c7 (2019-05-06). So the subscriber was compiled against the 0.6.0-era definition while the publisher ran the unreleased one. The 0.6.0 label for consumer_built_against is inferred from that md5 match and from the answerer's naming of 0.6.0 as the latest release installed under /opt/ros; the thread never states which franka_msgs headers the node was compiled against. A plausible mechanism, not confirmed in the thread: without franka_msgs in find_package the node picked up the released franka_msgs headers from /opt/ros/kinetic instead of the workspace's; the answerer found the fix unexplained. The answerer's first reading had the roles reversed (MoveRobot as a franka_ros client); the reporter corrected that MoveRobot is their own node. Only the added field and constants differ between the two definitions; no field was renamed, so element_retyped does not apply. The artifact's consumer sections quote the posted callback code and the connection record with both md5 fields removed; the record comes from the broken run, and it is repeated in the resolved section because the reporter changed only CMakeLists.txt. The provider section [[franka_ros@0.6.0]] holds FrankaState.msg and Errors.msg at tag 0.6.0 plus std_msgs/Header (std_msgs 0.5.11, Kinetic), laid out as a ROS 1 message_definition. The thread was read from the answers.ros.org static archive.
